summary: Backend regression for Buyer vs Seller workspace differentiation. 41/41 pytest cases PASS against the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Updated test_dashboard_stats_buyer to assert the new buyer payload (marketplace_listings, my_research_count, my_inquiries, watchlist_count, newsletters_received, aum_usd_b, exit_velocity_days, agent_success_rate, role='buyer'). Added 17 new tests covering: seller seed login + role, register endpoint accepting role='seller', dashboard stats seller payload (my_listings>=3, live_listings>=2, pipeline_value_usd_m, inbound_inquiries, my_campaigns/leads/newsletters), seller-only POST /api/listings (buyer => 403), seller seed listings (Helios live, Atlas live, Vertex draft), PATCH+DELETE own listings, /api/marketplace returns only status=live across sellers (Vertex draft NOT visible), /api/marketplace/{id} detail, POST /api/marketplace/{id}/inquire (inquiry_count increments), seller inbound vs buyer outbound /api/inquiries, PATCH /api/inquiries/{id}/status valid (reviewing) + invalid status 400 + buyer cannot patch (404 scoped by seller_id), watchlist GET/POST/DELETE incl. idempotent re-add and 404 on unknown listing. All pre-existing flows (auth, research, collateral, outreach draft+launch MOCKED, leads, newsletter draft+dispatch MOCKED, MCP, agents, composio, audit) still green.

minor.issue: When a non-seller (buyer) hits this endpoint with a valid inquiry id, the API returns 404 (not 403). This is technically safe (scoped by seller_id in the update query) but a 403 would be more semantically accurate and clearer for clients.

Accepts raw dict body (no Pydantic model), so the only validation is the in-handler tuple check. Consider adding an InquiryStatusUpdate Pydantic model with a Literal type for consistency with other endpoints.
Uses ListingCreate (full body) for partial updates — clients must resend all fields. Consider a ListingUpdate model with Optional fields for true PATCH semantics.
Admin/fallback branch still computes deals/leads/campaigns globally (no scoping), which may leak counts across tenants in a multi-tenant deployment. Not a bug for current single-tenant demo.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1270 lines — split into routers/ modules (auth, listings, marketplace, inquiries, watchlist, research, collateral, outreach, leads, newsletter, mcp, composio, audit) for maintainability.

POST /api/listings is correctly gated to seller/admin, but GET /api/listings is NOT gated — a buyer calling GET /api/listings gets back an empty list (because seller_id=user.id is a buyer) instead of a 403. Either gate it explicitly or rename to /api/listings/mine.
PATCH /api/inquiries/{id}/status returns 404 for both 'not found' and 'wrong owner' — fine for security-via-obscurity but consider distinguishing 403 vs 404 for cleaner API.
PATCH /api/inquiries/{id}/status takes body: dict (no Pydantic schema). Inconsistent with the rest of the codebase — add an InquiryStatusUpdate model.
PATCH /api/listings/{lid} reuses ListingCreate so a partial update forces clients to resend every field; add an Optional-field ListingUpdate model for proper PATCH semantics.
/api/watchlist/{lid} POST is idempotent but silently returns {'ok': True, 'already': True} — consider 200 vs 201 distinction or a clearer response shape.

Several Claude-backed POST endpoints (research, collateral, outreach draft, newsletter draft) remain synchronous, 15–35s each. Consider async job pattern (POST 202 + GET poll) — research currently ~33s of the 60s ingress budget.
safe_json_loads silently degrades to {'raw': raw} on parse failure; downstream code accesses data['company_name'] etc. without validation — add a 502 on missing essential fields.
CORS uses '*' with allow_credentials=True — combination is rejected by browsers; restrict to known origins.
seed_demo_user has no unique index on users.email — minor race risk across worker restarts; the find_one guard mitigates but a Mongo unique index would be cleaner.

rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs to RCA this iteration. The only behavior worth flagging is that PATCH /api/inquiries/{id}/status returns 404 (not 403) when a buyer tries to update an inquiry, because the update is scoped by seller_id in the Mongo filter; this is safe but semantically loose.
